data.name: GpuDefinitions
data.value: Source: NVML installed with the driver. VRAM is reported allocation, not activity or DXGI budget; reserved fields remain separate and the percentage is allocated / capacity. WDDM accounting depends on Windows and the driver. RTX 5060 power is a driver average of approximately 1 s. Memory clock is not effective transfer rate. Fan speed is not RPM; 0% may be fan-stop. Low utilization does not diagnose a bottleneck. Timestamps indicate local acquisition; internal sampling windows may differ.

data.value: Direct evidence of low availability under the local rule. Confidence about its cause and gaming impact: insufficient.

data.name: RamConfidenceLimited
data.value: Scope: observed physical availability. There is not enough evidence to recommend changes to Windows.

data.name: RamMethod
data.value: Local rule RAM-AVAIL-001 v1: low availability requires at most 10% of RAM and at most 1 GiB available continuously for 30 s. Very low: at most 5% and 512 MiB for 30 s. These are Lotus triage criteria, not official Windows limits. Missing readings never become zero.

data.name: RamCacheExplanation
data.value: Available does not mean only free RAM. Windows can repurpose standby/cache pages; cache occupancy does not prove mismanagement. Forcibly emptying working sets can cause new page faults when data is accessed again.

data.name: RamLimits
data.value: This version does not measure system commit, disk paging, compressed memory or per-application usage. It does not identify leaks or gaming bottlenecks. No page file, cache, process or Windows setting is changed.

data.name: BenchDetails
BenchMethod
data.value: PresentMon 2.6.0 / ETW. FPS = 1000 ÷ mean Present() interval; 1% low = 1000 ÷ mean slowest 1%. P95/P99 use nearest rank. Spikes exceed both 50 ms and 3× median. Minimum: 1,000 intervals and 10 s. The swap chain with most samples is used. This is not displayed FPS; generated frames can only be distinguished when identified by the source. The validated CSV does not report ETW loss counters. Generated-frame identification depends on game/driver instrumentation; Application may also mean an unidentified type.

data.name: Fq1Q
data.value: What does Lotus change in Windows?

data.name: Fq1A
data.value: Only what you confirm. The **game profile** adjusts the power plan and Windows gaming features; **DNS** switches your internet resolver; the **overlay** turns on the Lotus layout in RivaTuner. Temp files go to the **Recycle Bin** and programs close the normal way, like clicking X.

data.name: Fq2Q
data.value: How do I undo an optimization?

data.name: Fq2A
data.value: In **Optimize my PC**, use "Undo profile". DNS goes back in **Tools › Internet and DNS**, the overlay in **My Games › Back to previous layout**, and files can be restored from the Recycle Bin. Lotus only undoes if nothing else changed it since.

data.name: Fq3A
data.value: A live 0–100 score saying whether it's a good moment to play: free memory, processor load, graphics card temperature, heavy programs open and disk space. It only points out the problem and takes you to the right screen; it changes nothing on its own.

data.name: Fq4Q
data.value: Where does the game and Game list information come from?

data.name: Fq4A
data.value: From open sources: **Steam** (synopsis, genres, lists), **SteamSpy** (trending games and community tags), **Metacritic** (score, via Steam) and **GOG**. Difficulty is an **estimate** from the tags players give the game. Everything is kept on the PC so it works offline.

data.name: Fq5Q
data.value: What is Ctrl + Shift + L for?

data.name: Fq5A
data.value: With a game open, it runs a quick stutter check: a countdown shows in the overlay, Lotus measures and shows the most likely cause. The full result waits for you when you come back to Lotus.

data.name: Fq6Q
data.value: Does Lotus send my data anywhere?

data.name: Fq6A
data.value: No. Lotus only **downloads** public game and driver information. Your profile, favorites, notes, reports and measurements stay on this PC, in Documents › Lotus and the Lotus folder.

data.name: Fq7Q
data.value: Why does Lotus sometimes ask for administrator permission?

data.name: Fq7A
data.value: Lotus runs without privileges. When an action has to touch something system-wide (DNS, the RivaTuner overlay), a helper asks Windows for permission for that action only, and you can say no.
